items.title: Alex Bigard Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: I played about five years with him. ... I played with John Robichaud over there. Yeah, I played with, I played with the band himself.

ctx.x: Yeah. See, how'd you be going now? Where are your fans? Where did you get that idea from, huh? Well, that was all...

I was asking about the band at the Lyric Theater. What kind of a band it was, what they did there? Boy, at the Lyric Theater, they had a wonderful band over there. They used to play for the shows. And they had Andrew Kimball was playing trumpet. And Margaret Kimball, his wife, was playing piano. And they had Johnny Lindsay was playing trombone. And Red Happy was playing drum. And Lurie Nelson was playing clarinet. And old man John Robichaud, he was playing violin. He was the leader? He was the leader. Did they…

items.title: Alex Bigard Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] when you ever worked with Professor Mineta... [INTERVIEWEE] He was the leader.

ctx.x: Uh, uh, when Professor Mineta, uh, when you ever worked with Professor Mineta, uh, did you find that, uh, he, he sort of, uh, he was playing piano, did you say in that band? Oh, saxophone. Sax. Uh, did you find that he sort of led the band or, uh, or just played his part or? Oh, he was the leader of the band.
He was the leader. In other words, the old man, the violin was supposed to be the leader but Professor was
the, was the leader. Did, uh, Professor usually, uh, start the band and knock the band off? What's that? Did he usually start the band? Oh yeah, he start the band.
